RECORDED, NO VERDICT (judgment=true; 3.0.0_SA_CVO grades this at L9). Evidence with vintage:
(1) DID THE BRANCH RECOVER A HOLE IT DISCOVERED ITSELF -- the log's own lines, quoted: '03:45:38.389Z OK: wrote s3://opal-data-etfs/daily/cottonwood/2026-09-03.json (4 ETF slices, total_ownership=53750650.53, source_as_of=2026-09-03, ...)' then '03:45:38.391Z CATCHUP: processed 2026-09-03 (status=ok)'. The date was never supplied: the payload carried no `date` key, so the explicit-date branch at lambda_function.py:304-308 @ea47e92a72 was unreachable and the date was DISCOVERED by _catchup_missing_dates walking its reporting-obligation window.
(2) WHAT THE RESTORED SLICE DIFFERS IN -- NOTHING. sha256 060188a6e76b2275538e9cb2de0244023600ccfaa713fa738d6f24e2eb757cc8 on the pre-delete original, on the archive and on the restored object; ETag 212d7da63d847fd3f25facd6a651b481 on all three; 0 differences over 4 tickers x 8 fields = 32 cells. A byte-identical re-derivation, not merely an equivalent one -- consistent with _process_date being a pure function of the partition and the universe config (no generated_at inside the rows; it appears only in the log line at :252-254).
(3) WHAT THE BRANCH WOULD HAVE DONE WITH THE UPSTREAM PARTITION ABSENT -- it would have skipped the date and written nothing: :272-273 `if not _partition_exists(date_str): continue`, the never-fabricate skip. This was not reasoned hypothetically: 2026-09-09 IS that case inside the same window (probe: partition false, priced 0), and the run's own response shows it appearing in NONE of catchup_processed, catchup_failed or catchup_skipped_unpriced -- a date with no upstream partition is INVISIBLE in the response, so a silent skip and a healthy day are indistinguishable to a consumer reading only that response. Named for the CVO because it is a reporting property, not a defect I was sent to fix.
(4) WHAT THIS EXERCISE STILL DOES NOT PROVE: (i) A MULTI-DAY GAP -- exactly one date was deleted, so the loop ran with one recoverable member; nothing shows behaviour when several are missing, in particular whether a mid-loop _process_date failure leaves later dates unattempted (the try/except at :274-281 says it should not, but that is a code read, not an observation). (ii) A MULTI-PARTNER GAP -- only cottonwood was exercised; bd-49f-etf-ownership-daily is a separate function with its own ported loop and nothing here transfers to it by measurement. (iii) THE SCHEDULED FIRE ITSELF -- the rule's 10:30Z cron delivery was not observed; what is proven is that the target carries no payload override (1 of 1, all three keys absent) so the delivered envelope is the default one, and that the handler's branch selection depends only on the absence of date/probe. (iv) A GAP OLDER THAN THE WINDOW -- the window began 2026-09-01 because August's report has shipped (head-object rc 0, 252393 B, 2026-09-10T00:24:48Z), and a hole in a shipped month is outside it by design. (v) RECOVERY UNDER CONTENTION -- one fire, one hole, no concurrent producer run.
